content:
morgan: Quick heads-up — ran host-side p99 perf run after the kernel-selector change and we have a notable regression in parse+streaming overhead. p99 went from 82ms -> 142ms on the small-req tail. logs show more KV cache misses during handshake and a spike in small HTTP/2 writev syscalls.
lee: Ugh. Any idea which commit landed the kernel-selector tweak?
priya: It was the kselector v2 rollout from yesterday (PR #4928). I suspected batching heuristics might interact but didn't expect this level.
sam: Can you paste the flamegraph snippet or top stacks?
morgan: Snippet from perf (trimmed):
```
# time spent
20%  host-proxy  _parse_stream
12%  host-proxy  kv_cache_miss
10%  libc        writev (many small writes)
8%   kernel      select_kernel_variant
```
priya: That percent on kv_cache_miss aligns with a change we made to route small requests to the low-latency kernel. If the low-latency kernel increases K/V lookup churn, that could amplify misses.
anya: I ran a targeted repro — 1k small requests, 2 tokens each, http2 multiplexed. Baseline (pre-rollout): p99 88ms. With kselector v2: p99 148ms, KV hit ratio down ~6pp. Repro script: `./tools/repro --http2 --small-req --qps 200`
lee: Does the low-latency kernel change batching behavior? Might reduce batching window and increase number of tiny frames -> more writev.
sam: Yes, the kernel hints set batch_timeout to 0 in some paths for immediate dispatch. That reduces latency for single large requests but harms small-req throughput.
priya: Two options: revert kselector change (fast but loses other wins) or adjust batching heuristic to keep tiny writes coalesced for http2 path.
morgan: I also eyeballed trace IDs — a lot of these small writes are fragmenting the stream during initial tokenization. Tokenizer now returns chunks earlier due to preparse tweak.
anya: I can test: keep kselector v2 but force batch_timeout=2ms for http2 multiplex path. Quick A/B on canary would show if writev tail goes down.
ci-bot: deploy queued: canary/kselector-v2 -> staging at 3567801600 by priya (comment: running canary config with batching tweak) :rocket: 
lee: If canary shows improvement, we can promote with a patch that tweaks the heuristic. If not, revert and iterate.
sam: Action items: (1) anya to run canary with 2ms batch_timeout and send perf snapshot (2) morgan to correlate tokenization chunk timings with KV miss windows (3) priya to prepare revert PR if canary fails.
priya: ack. I'll monitor and post results in this thread.
morgan: Thanks — added to incident board as low-priority perf regression. Will follow up with flamegraphs once canary completes. :thumbsup:
